content.comment_body: In LSC, you can set the sensor type for analog functions, such as 0-10V, 0-20mA, 4-20mA, PT100/PT100, or choose 'No sensor'. What situations require using the 'No sensor' option?

Selecting 'No sensor' means no scaling is applied. The analog-to-digital converter on the input will convert any analog signal to a value between 0-1000 units. The selection mainly provides informational or parameterization assistance.

If your setup uses an analog amplifier, such as Analog Input -> Analog Amplifier -> other analog blocks, you only need to adjust the Analog Amplifier block. The other analog blocks should be set to 'No sensor'.
Thanks for the advice. After reviewing many [company_name] [product_name] example projects, I noticed that 'No sensor' is rarely chosen. I’ll give it a try.
If you do not need to change parameters, leaving the default settings or selecting 'No sensor', 0-10V, or 0-20mA will have the same effect. Only selecting 4-20mA modifies the default values.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for clarity on the role of the 'No sensor' option for analog input configuration in [product_name] software. The key takeaway is that 'No sensor' mainly impacts how parameters are presented, but does not alter the way analog signals are processed, unless a specific scaling option like 4-20mA is required. The fact that most example projects do not employ 'No sensor' adds to user confusion, highlighting the need for a better understanding of when each analog input type should be used.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward guidance on how and when to use the 'No sensor' setting for analog inputs, and want to understand its real effect on the operation of their programs.
